stimulus.text:
The Security Council as designed in the United Nations Charter, signed June 26, 1945.

| Members | Who they were | Power |
| 5 permanent members | United States, Soviet Union, Britain, France, China | Any one could veto a Council decision |
| 6 rotating members | Elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms | Voted, but held no veto |
stimulus.source_note: Table drawn from the design of the United Nations Charter (San Francisco, June 1945): five permanent members with the veto and six elected members in the original Council. The elected membership grew to ten in 1965.

source: original; stimulus drawn from book-grounded paraphrases, tables, and photographs (see source_note)
stem: Which nations held permanent seats on the Security Council as designed in 1945?

options.text: The United States, Germany, Japan, Italy, and Great Britain
options.misconception: Germany, Japan, and Italy were the defeated Axis powers, not permanent members.

options.text: The United States, the Soviet Union, Britain, France, and China
The United States, Canada, Brazil, India, and Australia
options.misconception: Canada, Brazil, India, and Australia could serve as rotating members, but they held no permanent seats.

options.text: The Soviet Union, Poland, Romania, Bulgaria, and Yugoslavia
options.misconception: Poland, Romania, Bulgaria, and Yugoslavia were not permanent members; the Soviet Union was the only one of these five that was.

rationales.A: Background from the books: Germany, Japan, and Italy were the defeated Axis powers, not permanent members.
rationales.B: The table names the five permanent members: the United States, the Soviet Union, Britain, France, and China.
rationales.C: Background from the books: Canada, Brazil, India, and Australia could serve as rotating members, but they held no permanent seats.
rationales.D: Background from the books: Poland, Romania, Bulgaria, and Yugoslavia were not permanent members; the Soviet Union was the only one of these five that was.
rationales.general:
1. The table names five permanent members of the Security Council.
2. They are the United States, the Soviet Union, Britain, France, and China.
3. Background: these were the leading Allied powers, and China held a seat even though its government was weak.
4. Each permanent member could veto a Council decision, so no action could pass against a great power's will.
Remember: the permanent seats went to the victors, not to every nation.
